newsitem.title: UK: UPS says international traffic top priority.
newsitem.headline: UPS says international traffic top priority.

text.p: United Parcel Service fully expects to maintain normal international traffic from Europe and other regions to the U.S., the company's European president, Randy Pulito said.
"International traffic is an all-important product and will be given number one priority in the U.S.," he told Reuters in a telephone interview from UPS' European Brussels headquarters.
He was commenting on the impact of the strike on international business by the company's 185,000 Teamster employees in the U.S. which began at 0400 GMT on Monday.
UPS handles some 700,000 packages daily in Europe with an export volume of 85,000 packages, with 10.5 percent of the latter representing exports to the U.S., Pulito added.
Inbound business to Europe accounted for 19.1 percent of worldwide international traffic, he said.

Transatlantic traffic will continue to be carried on UPS aircraft, Pulito said, adding: "As far as I am aware, right at this moment, they are still being flown by UPS pilots. However, if necessary they will be flown by management crews."
Asked whether the company's plans could deal with a long rather than a short strike, he said: "The contingency plans are set for the long-term.

"Europe has not been affected by the strike. There are no Teamsters here and all 24,000 employees in Europe have been working normally today," he added. -- Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
